revision.comment: [[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内の[[九十九王子]]旧蹟
revision.text:
'''九十九王子の旧蹟'''（くじゅうくおううじのきゅうせき）では、[[九十九王子|熊野九十九王子社]]の旧蹟のうち、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する旧蹟について述べる。
==九十九王子とは== ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[和歌山藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定され、旧蹟のみとなっている王子を扱う。
==九十九王子旧蹟== 泉佐野市内の九十九王子旧蹟は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。 ===鶴原王子=== '''鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
*所在地 泉佐野市貝田町 ===佐野王子=== '''佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
*所在地 泉佐野市上町
===籾井王子=== '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。1915年（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。
*所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井
==日根王子== '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[1250年]]（[[建長]]2年）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 --> ==参考文献== 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）
==関連事項== *[[熊野信仰]] *[[熊野古道]] - [[紀伊路]] *[[九十九王子]] **[[鞍持王子]] - '''鶴原王子''' - '''佐野王子''' - '''籾井（樫井）王子''' - [[厩戸王子]] **[[九十九王子の旧蹟 (貝塚市)]] - '''九十九王子の旧蹟 (泉佐野市)''' - [[九十九王子の旧蹟 (泉南市)]]

==日根王子== '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[1250年]]（[[建長]]2年）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 --> ==参考文献== 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）

'''九十九王子の旧蹟'''（くじゅうくおうじのきゅうせき）では、[[九十九王子|熊野九十九王子社]]の旧蹟のうち、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する旧蹟について述べる。
==九十九王子とは== ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[和歌山藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定され、旧蹟のみとなっている王子を扱う。
==九十九王子旧蹟== 泉佐野市内の九十九王子旧蹟は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。 ===鶴原王子=== '''鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
*所在地 泉佐野市貝田町 ===佐野王子=== '''佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
*所在地 泉佐野市上町
===籾井王子=== '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。
*所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井
==日根王子== '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[1250年]]（[[建長]]2年）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 --> ==参考文献== 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）

*所在地 泉佐野市貝田町 ===佐野王子=== '''佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
*所在地 泉佐野市上町
===籾井王子=== '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。

*所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井
==日根王子== '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[1250年]]（[[建長]]2年）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 --> ==参考文献== 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）

しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定され、旧蹟のみとなっている王子を扱う。
==九十九王子旧蹟== 泉佐野市内の九十九王子旧蹟は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。 ===鶴原王子=== '''鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
*所在地 泉佐野市貝田町 ===佐野王子=== '''佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
*所在地 泉佐野市上町
===籾井王子=== '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。
*所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井
==日根王子== '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[1250年]]（[[建長]]2年）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 --> ==参考文献== 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）
== 関連項目 == * [[熊野信仰]] * [[熊野古道]] - [[紀伊路]] * [[九十九王子]] ** （[[九十九王子の旧蹟 (貝塚市)#鞍持王子|鞍持王子]]） - '''鶴原王子''' - '''佐野王子''' - '''籾井（樫井）王子''' - （[[九十九王子の旧蹟 (泉南市)#厩戸王子|厩戸王子]]）

revision.comment: ページ [[九十九王子の旧蹟 (泉佐野市)]] を [[九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] へ移動: 改名提案にもとづく（see [[ノート:九十九王子]]）
revision.text:
{{改名提案|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|date=2009年8月|t=ノート:九十九王子}} '''九十九王子の旧蹟'''（くじゅうくおうじのきゅうせき）では、[[九十九王子|熊野九十九王子社]]の旧蹟のうち、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する旧蹟について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[承久]]3年（[[1221年]]）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定され、旧蹟のみとなっている王子を扱う。
== 九十九王子旧蹟 == 泉佐野市内の九十九王子旧蹟は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。
=== 鶴原王子 === '''鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
* 所在地 泉佐野市貝田町
=== 佐野王子 === '''佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
* 所在地 泉佐野市上町
=== 籾井王子 === '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。
* 所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井
== 日根王子 == '''日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[永保]]元年、[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[建長]]2年（[[1250年]]）の[[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 -->
== 参考文献 == 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）
== 関連項目 == * [[熊野信仰]] * [[熊野古道]] - [[紀伊路]] * [[九十九王子]] ** （[[九十九王子の旧蹟 (貝塚市)#鞍持王子|鞍持王子]]） - '''鶴原王子''' - '''佐野王子''' - '''籾井（樫井）王子''' - （[[九十九王子の旧蹟 (泉南市)#厩戸王子|厩戸王子]]）
{{九十九王子}}
[[Category:九十九王子の旧蹟|いすみさの]] [[Category:泉佐野市|くしゆうくおうしのきゆうせき]]

本項目では、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する'''九十九王子'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[承久]]3年（[[1221年]]）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定される王子を扱う。
== 九十九王子 == 泉佐野市内の九十九王子は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。
=== 鶴原王子 === ''' 鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
* 所在地 泉佐野市貝田町
=== 佐野王子 === ''' 佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治41年]]）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1929年]]（[[昭和24年]]）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
* 所在地 泉佐野市上町
=== 籾井王子 === '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正4年]]）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。
* 所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井

== 参考文献 == 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ：熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1）

== 日根王子 == ''' 日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[永保]]元年、[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[建長]]2年（[[1250年]]）の [[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 <!-- 日根神社（泉佐野市日根野）の近辺と推定する説もあるが、この場合、古道は市内東側・山際を通っていたことになる。前後にあたるはずの佐野王子はずっと海沿いに位置しており、日根神社説が正しいとすれば、道筋が変化したことによる衰退で退転したことになるだろう。 -->

本項目では、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する'''九十九王子'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[承久]]3年（[[1221年]]）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定される王子を扱う。
== 九十九王子 == 泉佐野市内の九十九王子は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。
=== 鶴原王子 === ''' 鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない
* 所在地 泉佐野市貝田町
=== 佐野王子 === ''' 佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治]]41年）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。
* 所在地 泉佐野市上町
=== 籾井王子 === '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。
『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。

本項目では、[[大阪府]][[泉佐野市]]内に所在する'''九十九王子'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。 == 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照'' 九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。 しかしながら、[[承久]]3年（[[1221年]]）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。 本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が大阪府泉佐野市内に推定される王子を扱う。 == 九十九王子 == 泉佐野市内の九十九王子は3社。さらに、詳細未詳の1社を挙げる。 === 鶴原王子 === ''' 鶴原王子'''（つるはらおうじ）は九十九王子の16番目。貝田王子の別称でも知られる。『泉州誌』『神祗史料』等の史料では、貝田社と加支田神社（泉佐野市鶴原）を同一視している。『泉佐野市史』には御幸記に鶴原王子の名で登場する旨の記述があるが、所在地の考定はない * 所在地 泉佐野市貝田町 === 佐野王子 === ''' 佐野王子'''（さのおうじ）は九十九王子の17番目。[[1908年]]（[[明治]]41年）、春日神社（泉佐野市春日町）に合祀され廃絶する。現在、比定地と推定されている場所には顕彰碑があるが、これは[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）[[4月]]に建てられたものである。 * 所在地 泉佐野市上町 File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|佐野王子跡の顕彰碑（大阪府泉佐野市上町一丁目）
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === 籾井王子 === '''籾井王子'''（もみいおうじ）は九十九王子の18番目。[[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）、日枝神社（泉佐野市南中樫井）に合祀され廃絶する。比定地には自動車販売・整備会社の社屋が建ち、その裏手の個人宅内に顕彰碑が建てられている（見学可能）。 『泉州誌』には樫居王子、『和泉誌』には籾井王子の記載がある。大阪府の史蹟名勝指定にあたっての考定によれば、『和泉誌』の籾井の表記は誤転記であり、本来は樫の邦字であるとしている。 * 所在地 泉佐野市南中樫井 == 日根王子 == ''' 日根王子'''（ひねおうじ）は、[[藤原為房]]の参詣記（[[永保]]元年、[[1081年]]）に記録があり、社殿・堂があったことが伝えられている王子。史料上で確認できる[[紀伊路]]でおそらくは最古の王子だが、これを最後に記録が途絶えている。[[建長]]2年（[[1250年]]）の [[後嵯峨院]]の第1回御幸の頃には廃絶していたようであり、比定地も和泉国日根郡日根郷にあったと推定されるにとどまり、詳細は定かではない。そのため、本項では番外として扱う。 == 参考文献 == 西 律、1987、『熊野古道みちしるべ - 熊野九十九王子現状踏査録』、荒尾成文堂（みなもと選書1） == 関連項目 == * [[熊野信仰]] * [[熊野古道]] - [[紀伊路]] * [[九十九王子]] ** （[[九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)#鞍持王子|鞍持王子]]） - '''鶴原王子''' - '''佐野王子''' - '''籾井王子''' - （[[九十九王子 (泉南市)#厩戸王子|厩戸王子]]） {{九十九王子}} {{DEFAULTSORT:くしゆうくおうし}} [[Category:九十九王子|いすみさの]] [[Category:大阪府の神社|くしゆうくおうしいすみさの]] [[Category:泉佐野市の歴史]]

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:new pages]][[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|Kuramochi Ōji|ja|鞍持王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|Umayado Ōji|ja|厩戸王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:new pages]][[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|Kuramochi Ōji|ja|鞍持王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|Umayado Ōji|ja|厩戸王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {| class="navbox mw-collapsible" ! colspan="10" style="background:#33ff99" |{{Tnavbar-collapsible| [[九十九王子]]一覧 |九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}} |- | style="background:#99ffff" |（{{ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}}） | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | |} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[Category:S]][[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:qq]]{{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

[[Category:new pages]][[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|Kuramochi Ōji|ja|鞍持王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {| class="navbox mw-collapsible" ! colspan="10" style="background:#33ff99" |{{Tnavbar-collapsible| |九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}} |- | style="background:#99ffff" |（{{ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}}） | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | |} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[Category:S]][[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:qq]]{{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {| class="navbox mw-collapsible" ! colspan="10" style="background:#33ff99" |{{Tnavbar-collapsible| |九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}} |- | style="background:#99ffff" |（{{ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}}） | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | |} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:new pages]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:new pages]] [[Category:qq]]{{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {| class="navbox mw-collapsible" ! colspan="10" style="background:#33ff99" |{{Tnavbar-collapsible| |九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}} |- | style="background:#99ffff" |（{{ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}}） | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | | style="background:#FFFFFF" | |} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:unsorted completion categories]] {{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

[[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-{{subst:MAINSPACE}}--qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-{{subst:MAINSPACE}}--qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-{{subst:MAINSPACE}}--qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] {{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ** ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] {{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:subst:NAMESPACE]] [[Category:subst:MAINSPACE]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] {{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:subst:NAMESPACE]] [[Category:Subst:NAMESPACE]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] {{Kujūku Ōji|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:ppp]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' - '''Sano Ōji''' - '''Momii Ōji''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (泉南市)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] {{citation needed|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:ppp]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] {{Kujūku Ōji}} [[ja:List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the shrines in the region of 泉佐野市. [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] ==Overview== == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' (Sennan City)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} [[Category:Kujukuōji]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano City]] This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|泉佐野市}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-List of Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto
