This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ_Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Sennan City)|ja|九十九王子 (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子}}) {{Kujukuōji}} ''' ==[[Kujūku Ōji template|List of the 99 Oji]]== {{citation needed|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|ill|Jōnan-gū|en}}{{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|lt=Nachi Taisha}} [[Category:神社関連テンプレート|くしゆくおうし]] [[Category:九十九王子|-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-泉佐野市)-qq]] [[en:泉佐野市)]]'''[[Category:Kujukuōji]]''' [[Category:qq---qq]] '''[[Category:History of Izumisano City]]''' [[Category:qq-泉佐野市)-qq]] {{citation needed|bottom}}[[Category:sqq]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks]] [[Category:Kujūku Ōji template forks on groups]] [[Category:100 shortest pages as of February 11 2025]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qqq]][[en:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] ]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]][[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[Category:ppp]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]][[sn:泉佐野市)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]][[ja:泉佐野市)]][[Category:11]] {{Kujūku Ōji}} [[ja:泉佐野市)]]

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-泉佐野市)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[Category:qq deprecated open]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4qq7|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4qq7|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4qq7|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4qq7|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}) - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子}}''' - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221年}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year }}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year }}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市}} [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year }}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year|12=draft}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|12=draft}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇|12=draft}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}} - ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市|12=draft}} == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year|12=draft}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市|12=draft}} == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year|12=draft}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|12=draft}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇|12=draft}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}} - This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Izumisano City|ja|泉佐野市|12=draft}} == Kujukuōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''Kujukuōji''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Kujukuōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.'' Kujukuōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[12th century]] to the [[13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[Jōkyū Rebellion]] in {{ill|1221|ja|1221st year|12=draft}}, pilgrimages from [[Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[Kishu Domain]] during the [[Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[Meiji period]], the [[State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Kujukuōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Kujukuōji == There are three Kujukuōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Kujukuōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Kujukuōji. In [[1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|12=draft}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|ja|後嵯峨天皇|12=draft}} in [[1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Kujukuōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}} - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kujukuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}} ''' ({{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|12=draft}}) * '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=List of Kujūku Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|12=draft}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|12=draft}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Kujūku Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|12=draft}}''' -
