{{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Faith|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Three Shrines|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} * [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]] - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} * {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} ''' ({{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}) * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' - ({{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Sennan City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Sennan City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}) {{Ninety-Nine Ōji}} ''' ==References== {{reflist}} '''''' '''''' {{Ninety-Nine Ōji}} {{translated page|ja|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|version=75991280|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Lists of Ninety-Nine Ōji]] }} [[sn:List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)]] [[sn:-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[sn:泉佐野市)]] [[ja:泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano, Osaka]] --> [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano, Osaka]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]]

{{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Faith|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Three Shrines|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} * [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]] - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} * {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} ''' ({{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Kuramochi Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}) * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Kaizuka)|en|lt=Tsuruhara Ōji|error=九十九王子 (岸和田市・貝塚市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Sano Ōji|error=佐野王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (泉佐野市)}}''' * '''{{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji (泉佐野市)|en|lt=Momii Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' - ({{ill|List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Sennan City)|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji (泉南市)|en|lt=Umayado Ōji|error=九十九王子 (泉南市)|oji=王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Sennan City)|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}) {{Ninety-Nine Ōji}} ''' ==References== {{reflist}} '''''' '''''' {{Ninety-Nine Ōji}} {{translated page|ja|九十九王子 (泉佐野市)|version=75991280|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Lists of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines]] }} [[sn:List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)]] [[sn:-てんふれえと]] [[ja:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[zh:九十九王子 (泉佐野市)]] [[sn:泉佐野市)]] [[ja:泉佐野市)]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano, Osaka]] --> [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Izumisano, Osaka]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] [[Category:qq]][[en:List of Ninety-Nine Ōji (Izumisano City)]][[Category:qq]]

{{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Faith|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Three Shrines|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} * [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]] - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii {{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrine (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō (Minamoto Selection 1) == See Also == * {{ill|Kumano Faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Faith|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Three Shrines|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山}} * [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]] - {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii {{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shriness'', Arao Seibundō This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō {{Infobox religious building|prefecture={{ill|Izumisano|qid=Q852018}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.4117|N|135.3251|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11370048]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:52, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)

This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Izumisano|Izumisano City]] == Ninety-Nine Ōji in Izumisano City == This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|fr|Kujūkuōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji}}''' (九十九王子) located within [[Izumisano City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. == What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For details, see {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.'' Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shrines|Shrines]] located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]], particularly along the {{ill|Kii Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kii Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}, rapidly organized mainly during the [[:en:12th century|12th century]] to the [[:en:13th century|13th century]] by Kumano Shugendō practitioners who served as guides for imperial family members and nobility on their pilgrimages to Kumano. These shrines were dedicated to praying for the protection of pilgrims. However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū Rebellion|Jōkyū Rebellion]] in [[:en:1221|1221]], pilgrimages from [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]] declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of the Kii Route. This trend continued through the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Even though efforts to honor these shrines were made by the [[:en:Kishu Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they could not regain their former significance. Additionally, after the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]], the [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] movement and urbanization led to the consolidation and abolishment of many shrines, resulting in the loss of original sites and the obscurity of exact locations. This article covers the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines presumed to be located within Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. == Ninety-Nine Ōji == There are three Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines in Izumisano City, with an additional shrine of uncertain details. === Tsuruhara Ōji === '''Tsuruhara Ōji''' (鶴原王子) is the 16th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. It is also known as Kaida Ōji. Historical records such as the ''Senshū-shi'' and ''Jingi Shiryō'' identify it with Kashida Shrine in Tsuruhara, Izumisano City. ''Izumisano City History'' mentions its appearance in the ''Gokōki,'' but the exact location remains unidentified. * Location: Kaida-chō, Izumisano City === Sano Ōji === '''Sano Ōji''' (佐野王子) is the 17th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1908|1908]] (Meiji 41), it was consolidated into Kasuga Shrine in Kasuga-chō, Izumisano City, and subsequently abolished. A commemorative monument now stands at the presumed site, erected in [[:en:1945|1945]] (Shōwa 20). * Location: Kamimachi, Izumisano City File:Ruins of Sano-oji Shrine.JPG|Commemorative monument at the site of Sano Ōji (Kamimachi 1-chome, Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture)
{{Coord|34.4117|135.3251|format=dms|dscale:30000}} === Momii Ōji === '''Momii Ōji''' (籾井王子) is the 18th of the Ninety-Nine Ōji. In [[:en:1915|1915]] (Taishō 4), it was consolidated into Hie Shrine in Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City, and abolished. The presumed location now hosts a car dealership, with a commemorative monument erected behind a private residence (accessible for viewing). The ''Senshū-shi'' refers to it as Kashii Ōji, while the ''Izumi-shi'' refers to it as Momii Ōji. According to Osaka Prefecture's designation of historical sites, the "Momii" notation in ''Izumi-shi'' is likely a transcription error, originally referring to "Kashi." * Location: Minami-Naka-Kashii, Izumisano City == Hine Ōji == '''Hine Ōji''' (日根王子) is recorded in the pilgrimage diary of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamefusa|ja|藤原為房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tamefusa|1=Fujiwara no Tamefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623393}} (Eihō 1, 1081), mentioning the existence of shrine buildings and halls. It is likely the oldest Ōji along the [[Kii Route]] based on historical records, but no further records exist after this mention. By the time of the first pilgrimage of [[:en:Emperor Go-Saga|Emperor Go-Saga]] in [[:en:1250|1250]] (Kenchō 2), it appears to have been abolished. Its presumed location is in Hine-gō, Hine District, Izumi Province, though exact details remain unclear. Hence, it is treated as an extra entry here. == References == Nishi Ritsu, 1987, ''Kumano Kodo Michishirube - A Field Survey of the Present Status of the Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines'', Arao Seibundō
